metadata.source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED) & CDS SIMBAD Astronomical Database
metadata.description: Verified astrometric positions, spectroscopic redshifts, morphological classifications, distance estimates from NASA/IPAC NED, and authentic NASA/ESA mission observations with zero image duplication.

records.name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
records.distanceMethod: Cepheid Leavitt Law & Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB)
records.description: The largest galaxy in the Local Group, heading toward a gravitational merger with our Milky Way in ~4.5 billion years.
records.scientificSignificance: Primary extragalactic laboratory for stellar population synthesis, Cepheid distance calibration, and dark matter halo dynamics.

image.title: Andromeda Galaxy Across Wavelengths
image.caption: Multi-spectral composite revealing Andromeda's spiral arms traced by hot young stars (blue, UV) and cool interstellar dust (orange, infrared).

images.title: Andromeda Galaxy Across Wavelengths (GALEX/Spitzer/WISE)
images.caption: Multi-spectral composite revealing Andromeda's spiral arms traced by hot young stars (blue, UV) and cool interstellar dust (orange, infrared).

images.title: Andromeda Far-Infrared Dust Ring & Relativistic Core
images.caption: Herschel Space Observatory far-infrared scan exposing the 75,000-light-year ring of cold dust where new stars condense at temperatures barely above absolute zero.

records.name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
records.description: The third-largest member of the Local Group, rich in giant ionized hydrogen star-forming regions such as NGC 604.
records.scientificSignificance: Serves as an archetype of unbarred late-type spirals with pure exponential disks and minimal central bulge.

image.title: M33: Ultraviolet Portrait of the Triangulum Galaxy
image.caption: Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) ultraviolet mosaic mapping energetic radiation from hot O and B class stars in the loose spiral arms of M33.

images.title: M33: Ultraviolet Portrait of the Triangulum Galaxy (GALEX)
images.caption: Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) ultraviolet mosaic mapping energetic radiation from hot young stars.

images.title: Spitzer Space Telescope Infrared Mosaic of M33
images.caption: Infrared imaging exposing the organic emission and cool silicate dust along the spiral arms of M33.

records.name: Whirlpool Galaxy (M51a)
records.distanceMethod: Type II-P Supernova Standard Candle & TRGB
records.description: A classic grand-design spiral galaxy tidally interacting with its companion dwarf galaxy NGC 5195.
records.scientificSignificance: The premier laboratory for density wave theory, spiral shock fronts, and tidal interaction-induced starbursts.

image.title: Whirlpool Galaxy Great Observatories Composite (M51)
image.caption: Great Observatories composite combining Hubble optical, Chandra X-ray, and Spitzer infrared data to unveil the grand-design spiral structure and companion NGC 5195.

observationalMetadata.telescope: Spitzer Space Telescope & Hubble Space Telescope

images.title: Whirlpool Galaxy Great Observatories Composite (M51)
images.caption: Hubble optical, Chandra X-ray, and Spitzer infrared composite.
images.instrument: Hubble ACS, Chandra ACIS, Spitzer IRAC

records.name: Sombrero Galaxy (M104)
records.description: Characterized by an exceptionally luminous white central bulge and a prominent dark absorption lane of interstellar dust.
records.scientificSignificance: Hosts one of the most massive central black holes (~1 billion solar masses) in nearby spiral galaxies and an anomalously large globular cluster system.

image.title: Sombrero Galaxy Infrared Portrait (M104, Spitzer)
image.caption: Spitzer Space Telescope infrared view revealing the Sombrero galaxy as a split personality: an elliptical galaxy with an embedded thin disk of star-forming dust.

images.title: Sombrero Galaxy Infrared Portrait (M104, Spitzer)
images.caption: Spitzer infrared imaging exposing the embedded disk and massive stellar bulge.

records.name: Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC)
records.description: A major satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, housing the Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus), the most active starburst nursery in the Local Group.
records.scientificSignificance: The fundamental first rung and anchor of the extragalactic cosmic distance ladder.

image.title: Large Magellanic Cloud Infrared Mosaic (Herschel/Spitzer)
image.caption: Herschel Space Observatory and Spitzer Space Telescope far-infrared mosaic of the Large Magellanic Cloud showing cool interstellar dust filaments and 30 Doradus.

images.title: Large Magellanic Cloud Infrared Mosaic (Herschel/Spitzer)
images.caption: Herschel and Spitzer far-infrared mosaic of cosmic dust clouds.

records.name: Pinwheel Galaxy (M101)
records.description: A face-on spiral galaxy twice the diameter of our Milky Way containing massive young star clusters and prominent spiral arms.
records.scientificSignificance: Critical target for studying abundance gradients across spiral disks and host to SN 2011fe (Type Ia) and SN 2023ixf (Type II).

image.title: Pinwheel Galaxy Multiwavelength Composite (M101)
image.caption: Multiwavelength composite combining Chandra (X-ray, purple), GALEX (UV, blue), Hubble (optical, yellow), and Spitzer (IR, red) across the face-on spiral M101.

images.title: Pinwheel Galaxy Multiwavelength Composite (M101)
images.caption: Chandra X-ray, GALEX UV, Hubble optical, and Spitzer infrared data.
images.instrument: Chandra ACIS, GALEX, Hubble ACS, Spitzer IRAC

records.name: Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC)
records.description: A close satellite dwarf galaxy of the Milky Way undergoing severe tidal disruption from gravitational interaction with the LMC.
records.scientificSignificance: Where Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered the period-luminosity relation in Cepheids in 1908, enabling cosmic distance measurements.

image.title: Small Magellanic Cloud Infrared Portrait (Herschel/Spitzer)
image.caption: Herschel and Spitzer far-infrared mosaic exposing the stellar bar and dusty wing of dwarf irregular galaxy SMC.

images.title: Small Magellanic Cloud Infrared Portrait (Herschel/Spitzer)
images.caption: Far-infrared composite capturing dust emission in the low-metallicity SMC.

records.name: Sculptor Galaxy (NGC 253)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) & Cepheids
records.description: A dusty edge-on spiral galaxy in the Sculptor Group experiencing furious starburst activity and superwinds in its nuclear core.
records.scientificSignificance: Benchmark nearby target for high-energy cosmic ray acceleration, galactic superwinds, and interstellar dust outflow mechanics.

image.title: Sculptor Galaxy Infrared Portrait (NGC 253, Spitzer)
image.caption: Spitzer Space Telescope infrared mosaic charting the intense starburst nucleus and dense dust lanes of NGC 253.

images.title: Sculptor Galaxy Infrared Portrait (NGC 253, Spitzer)
images.caption: Infrared imaging exposing starburst activity and dust disk.

records.name: Barred Spiral Prototype NGC 1300
records.description: Widely recognized as the textbook definition of a barred spiral galaxy, with a central bar stretching over 50,000 light-years.
records.scientificSignificance: Exhibits a 'nucleus within a nucleus'—a secondary nuclear ring structure rotating in the core with its own miniature spiral arms.

image.title: Barred Spiral Galaxy NGC 1300 (Hubble ACS)
image.caption: Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys optical portrait resolving dust filaments and young star clusters along NGC 1300 central bar.

images.title: Barred Spiral Galaxy NGC 1300 (Hubble ACS)
images.caption: Optical ACS observation of grand-design barred spiral.
images.wavelength: B, V, I optical filters (435–814 nm)

records.name: Southern Pinwheel (Messier 83)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) & Cepheids
records.description: A nearby grand-design barred spiral dubbed the 'Supernova Factory' due to six recorded historical supernovae within a century.
records.scientificSignificance: GALEX discovery of an enormous extended ultraviolet (XUV) disk four times the size of the optical galaxy.

image.title: Southern Pinwheel Galaxy in Infrared (M83, WISE)
image.caption: Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer 4-band infrared mosaic tracing spiral arm star clusters and warm dust lanes in Messier 83.

images.title: Southern Pinwheel Galaxy in Infrared (M83, WISE)
images.caption: Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer mosaic.

records.name: Messier 87 (Virgo A)
records.distanceMethod: Surface Brightness Fluctuations (SBF) & Globular Cluster Luminosity
records.description: The giant dominant elliptical galaxy at the center of the Virgo Cluster, host to a 6.5-billion-solar-mass supermassive black hole.
records.scientificSignificance: Home to the first directly imaged black hole shadow (Event Horizon Telescope) and a 5,000-light-year relativistic plasma jet.

image.title: Giant Elliptical Messier 87 & Relativistic Jet (Spitzer IR)
image.caption: Spitzer Space Telescope infrared observation showing shockwaves created by the relativistic jet launched from M87 supermassive black hole.

images.title: Giant Elliptical Messier 87 & Relativistic Jet (Spitzer IR)
images.caption: Spitzer infrared portrait of M87 and relativistic jet.

records.name: Young Elliptical Galaxy (NGC 3610)
records.distanceMethod: Surface Brightness Fluctuations (SBF) & Globular Cluster Luminosity
records.description: A prominent young elliptical galaxy exhibiting fine shell structures and an internal stellar disk resulting from a major galactic merger ~4 billion years ago.
records.scientificSignificance: Primary archetype for studying the formation of elliptical galaxies through disk galaxy mergers and remnant shell dynamics.

image.title: Hubble Views a Young Elliptical Galaxy (NGC 3610)
image.caption: Hubble Space Telescope optical observation capturing the luminous core and faint concentric shell remnants of elliptical galaxy NGC 3610.

images.title: Hubble Views a Young Elliptical Galaxy (NGC 3610)
images.caption: Hubble Space Telescope optical observation capturing concentric merger shell remnants in NGC 3610.

records.name: Elliptical Galaxy NGC 2768
records.description: An elongated elliptical galaxy featuring a luminous central core fading outwards to a smooth stellar haze, crossed by a prominent perpendicular dust lane.
records.scientificSignificance: Laboratory for studying polar rings of gas and dust acquired through accretion from neighbor galaxies in an early-type system.

image.title: Hubble Peers Through the Elliptical Haze (NGC 2768)
image.caption: Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys view revealing the central dust lane and luminous halo of elliptical galaxy NGC 2768.

images.title: Hubble Peers Through the Elliptical Haze (NGC 2768)
images.caption: Hubble Space Telescope view of the luminous core and dust lane of NGC 2768.

records.name: Centaurus A (NGC 5128)
records.description: The closest active radio galaxy to Earth, featuring a prominent warped dust belt bisecting a luminous elliptical galaxy.
records.scientificSignificance: Direct evidence of a past major merger between a giant elliptical and a smaller spiral, powering colossal radio lobe lobes across 8 degrees of the sky.

image.title: Active Galaxy Centaurus A Multi-wavelength View
image.caption: Chandra X-ray (blue) and VLT optical (orange) composite showing relativistic jets and prominent dust belt bisecting Centaurus A.

images.title: Active Galaxy Centaurus A Multi-wavelength View
images.caption: Chandra X-ray and VLT optical observation.

records.name: Antennae Galaxies (NGC 4038/4039)
records.morphologicalType: SA(s)m pec / SA(s)m pec (Colliding Interacting Pair)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) in Tidal Tail
records.description: Two spiral galaxies undergoing a violent high-speed collision, hurling long tidal streams of stars and gas resembling insect antennae.
records.scientificSignificance: The youngest and nearest prototype of major galaxy collisions; exhibits over 1,000 young super star clusters created in shock fronts.

image.title: Antennae Galaxies Colliding (Hubble/Chandra/Spitzer)
image.caption: Great Observatories composite showing galactic collision between NGC 4038 and NGC 4039 triggering starburst knots and expansive tidal tails.

images.title: Antennae Galaxies Colliding (Hubble/Chandra/Spitzer)
images.caption: Great Observatories multiwavelength composite.
images.instrument: Hubble ACS, Chandra ACIS, Spitzer IRAC

records.name: Cigar Galaxy (Messier 82)
records.distanceMethod: Tip of the Red Giant Branch (TRGB) & Cepheids
records.description: An edge-on starburst galaxy with enormous bipolar plumes of glowing hydrogen gas driven out of the disk by collective supernova winds.
records.scientificSignificance: Forms stars at a rate 10 times faster than the Milky Way due to recent tidal encounters with M81.

image.title: Cigar Galaxy Starburst Core & Superwind (M82)
image.caption: Hubble Space Telescope and Spitzer Space Telescope composite showing glowing hydrogen gas superwind ejected perpendicular to M82 disk.

images.title: Cigar Galaxy Starburst Core & Superwind (M82)
images.caption: Hubble and Spitzer composite of superwind plumes.

records.name: Cartwheel Galaxy (ESO 350-40)
records.description: A spectacular bullseye ring galaxy produced when a smaller companion galaxy plunged directly through its center like a stone in water.
records.scientificSignificance: The expanding density shock wave created a sparkling ring of intense star formation expanding outward at over 200,000 km/h.

image.title: Cartwheel Galaxy Ring Expansion (Chandra/Hubble/Spitzer/GALEX)
image.caption: Great Observatories composite showing cosmic collision ripple expanding at over 200,000 mph through the Cartwheel Galaxy ring.

images.title: Cartwheel Galaxy Ring Expansion
images.caption: Multiwavelength composite tracing the expanding starburst shock ring.
images.instrument: Chandra ACIS, Hubble WFPC2, GALEX, Spitzer IRAC

records.name: Messier 77 (NGC 1068)
records.description: A bright barred spiral containing an energetic active galactic nucleus (AGN) completely shrouded by a dense dusty torus.
records.scientificSignificance: The fundamental prototype for the Unified Model of Active Galactic Nuclei; spectropolarimetry confirmed the presence of hidden broad emission lines.

image.title: NuSTAR High-Energy X-Ray View of Seyfert 2 Galaxy M77
image.caption: NuSTAR high-energy X-ray observation penetrating the obscuring gas cloud surrounding the active galactic nucleus of Messier 77 (NGC 1068).

images.title: NuSTAR High-Energy X-Ray View of Seyfert 2 Galaxy M77
images.caption: High-energy X-ray view of active galactic nucleus.

records.name: Quasar 3C 273
records.angularSize: Point source core with 20″ relativistic jet
records.description: The first quasar ever identified (Maarten Schmidt, 1963) and one of the most luminous active galactic nuclei in the observable universe.
records.scientificSignificance: Luminosity exceeds 4 trillion suns, fueled by a central black hole of 880 million solar masses consuming 100 Earth masses per second.

image.title: Quasar 3C 273 X-Ray Jet (HEAO-2 / Einstein Observatory)
image.caption: Historic X-ray imaging from the Einstein Observatory (HEAO-2) resolving the high-energy jet launched by quasar 3C 273.

images.title: Quasar 3C 273 X-Ray Jet (HEAO-2 / Einstein Observatory)
images.caption: X-ray observation of the relativistic plasma jet.

records.name: Markarian 231 (UGC 08058)
records.description: The nearest Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxy (ULIRG) to Earth, radiating 99% of its colossal energy in the infrared due to dust obscuration.
records.scientificSignificance: Proposed to host a close binary supermassive black hole system producing powerful molecular outflows clearing cold gas from the host galaxy.

image.title: Markarian 231 Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidate
image.caption: NuSTAR and Chandra X-ray observations tracking extreme relativistic accretion disk emission in ultraluminous infrared galaxy Mrk 231.

images.title: Markarian 231 Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidate
images.caption: High-energy X-ray spectrum and imaging.

records.name: Virgo Cluster Core (M87 Subgroup)
records.distanceMethod: Mean SBF and TRGB of ~2,000 member galaxies
records.description: The massive heart of the Virgo Supercluster containing over 2,000 cataloged galaxies bound in a common gravitational potential.
records.scientificSignificance: Its colossal gravitational pull creates the 'Virgo-centric infall' where the Local Group and Milky Way are pulled toward the cluster at ~250 km/s.

image.title: Virgo Galaxy Cluster Multi-wavelength Mosaic
image.caption: Wide-field GALEX ultraviolet and Spitzer infrared mosaic spanning the core of the Virgo Cluster, anchored by giant elliptical Messier 87.

images.title: Virgo Galaxy Cluster Multi-wavelength Mosaic
images.caption: GALEX UV and Spitzer IR wide-field mosaic.

records.name: Coma Cluster (Abell 1656)
records.description: One of the densest known galactic concentrations containing over 1,000 identified galaxies dominated by giant ellipticals NGC 4874 and NGC 4889.
records.scientificSignificance: Where Fritz Zwicky discovered dark matter in 1933 by applying the virial theorem to member orbital velocities.

image.title: Coma Galaxy Cluster Infrared Panoramic (Abell 1656)
image.caption: Spitzer Space Telescope infrared mosaic containing over a thousand galaxies locked in a colossal gravitational well 320 million light-years away.

images.title: Coma Galaxy Cluster Infrared Panoramic (Abell 1656)
images.caption: Spitzer Space Telescope infrared mosaic.

records.name: Stephan's Quintet (HCG 92)
records.description: A celebrated compact group of five galaxies, four of which are locked in an intricate gravitational dance generating massive shockwaves.
records.scientificSignificance: Features an enormous shock wave larger than the Milky Way produced as galaxy NGC 7318b plunges through the intra-group medium at millions of km/h.

image.title: Stephan's Quintet Compact Group (Hubble WFPC2)
image.caption: Hubble Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 optical portrait of compact galaxy group Hickson 92, exhibiting tidal tails and gravitational shock fronts.

images.title: Stephan's Quintet Compact Group (Hubble WFPC2)
images.caption: Hubble WFPC2 optical imaging.

records.name: SMACS J0723.3-7327 (JWST First Deep Field)
records.description: A massive galaxy cluster whose immense gravitational field acts as a natural cosmic lens, bending and magnifying the light of galaxies behind it.
records.scientificSignificance: The historic first operational deep-field image from JWST, revealing galaxies as they existed over 13.1 billion years ago.

image.title: SMACS J0723.3-7327 (Webb's First Deep Field)
image.caption: James Webb Space Telescope NIRCam infrared deep field revealing massive gravitational lensing arcs from early galaxies over 13 billion years in the past.

images.title: SMACS J0723.3-7327 (Webb's First Deep Field)
images.caption: JWST NIRCam infrared deep field.
